subject: general
question: A person is standing in a bus that suddenly stops. The person tends to fall forward. Which of the following laws of motion is directly responsible for this phenomenon?

options.text: The Law of Conservation of Momentum.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's First Law of Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**, also known as the Law of Inertia, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• When the bus suddenly stops, the body of the person inside the bus tends to continue moving forward due to inertia, as no external force initially acts directly on their body to stop this motion.
 
• The phenomenon occurs because the lower part of the person’s body comes to rest due to contact with the bus floor, while the upper part continues moving forward until balanced by external forces like friction or a physical obstruction.
 
• This tendency of the body to resist changes to its state of motion directly illustrates Newton's First Law.* Hence, this law is responsible for the phenomenon described in the question.*
 
• Other laws of motion like Newton's Second and Third Laws are not directly applicable here as they deal with acceleration due to force and action-reaction pairs, respectively.
